title: Frame scheme of a finite etale local system
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $\ell$ be a prime, put $A=\mathbf Z/\ell\mathbf Z$, and let $n\geq0$. On the small etale site $T_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], let $H$ be a sheaf of $\underline A_T$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] which on an etale cover is isomorphic to $\underline{A^n}_T$. For every morphism of schemes $v:U\to T$, write $v^{-1}H$ for its inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] and set
$$\operatorname{Fr}_H(U)=\operatorname{Isom}_{\underline A_U}(\underline{A^n}_U,v^{-1}H).$$
Restriction along $w:U'\to U$ is inverse image of the isomorphism, followed by the canonical constant-sheaf and composite-inverse-image comparisons. There is a finite etale surjective scheme $p:P\to T$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category] and a universal frame $\lambda_P:\underline{A^n}_P\xrightarrow{\sim}p^{-1}H$ such that pullback of $\lambda_P$ gives a bijection $\operatorname{Mor}_T(U,P)\cong\operatorname{Fr}_H(U)$, natural for all $T$-schemes $U$. For every $v:U\to T$, the scheme $P\times_TU$ [def-pc-fibre-product] with its pulled-back universal frame represents $\operatorname{Fr}_{v^{-1}H}$ over $U$, compatibly with composition of base changes. On each etale chart $U\to T$ trivializing $H$, the representing scheme is the disjoint union of copies of $U$ indexed by $\operatorname{GL}_n(A)$. Its fibre at every geometric point is the set of frames of the corresponding stalk of $H$. The empty base and $n=0$ are included.

source.place: Tag 03RV, lemma-characterize-finite-locally-constant; Tag 03Q1, lemma-stalk-pullback (4). Frame construction and arbitrary-test-scheme evaluation from returned proof Step 2; the argument and the existing inputs are preserved in report.md.

proof.text: Put $M=A^n$ and $G=\operatorname{Aut}_A(M)=\operatorname{GL}_n(A)$. This is a nonempty finite set: it contains the identity and embeds in the set of all functions from the finite set $M$ to itself. Define $F(V)=\operatorname{Isom}_{\underline A_V}(\underline M_V,H|_V)$ for etale $V\to T$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction] and [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image], restriction is canonically the inverse image used in the question, including the module structure; [lem-sfb-geometric-inverse-image-constant-module] identifies the restricted constant source with $\underline M_V$. Thus [lem-sf-local-module-isom-sheaf] makes $F$ a sheaf of sets, with exactly the question's restriction maps. The slice $T_{\mathrm{et}}/V$ is $V_{\mathrm{et}}$: composition and cancellation of etale morphisms give the identification [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation].

source.place: Tag 03S2, section-extension-by-zero (inverse image is restriction); Tag 03Q1, lemma-stalk-pullback; Tag 093T, sites-modules-lemma-locally-constant, proof of (2)

proof.text: On any scheme $V$, the canonical map $\underline G_V\to\mathcal Aut_{\underline A_V}(\underline M_V)$ sends $g$ to its constant module automorphism. It is an isomorphism as follows. Since $M$ is finite free, [lem-pur-site-constant-module-hom] identifies the endomorphism sheaf with $\underline{\operatorname{End}_A(M)}_V$, by the canonical constant-map comparison. Its underlying set sheaf is the constant set sheaf, by [def-sf-site-constant-module-functor] and [lem-pc-sites-sheafification-underlying-sets]. Given an automorphism and its inverse, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-constant-set-sections-cover] makes both constant, say $a,b$, on a common etale covering. On a nonempty member, injectivity of constant labels gives $ab=ba=1$, so $a\in G$; empty members have unique sections and impose no condition. This proves local surjectivity of the displayed map. The same injectivity on nonempty members proves local injectivity. Both sides are sheaves, so [lem-galois-set-sheaf-local-bijection-isomorphism] gives the claimed isomorphism. Its construction uses the same constant linear maps after restriction.

source.place: Tag 093T, lemma-locally-constant (1),(2), canonical Hom map and mutually inverse pairs

proof.text: Choose the given etale cover $t_i:T_i\to T$ and trivializations $\tau_i:\underline M_{T_i}\simeq t_i^{-1}H$. Composition $g\mapsto\tau_i\circ g$ and its inverse $\lambda\mapsto\tau_i^{-1}\circ\lambda$ identify $F|_{T_i}$ with $\underline G_{T_i}$ by Step 2. Hence $F$ is finite locally constant. Apply [lem-galois-flc-representable] to obtain a finite etale $p:P\to T$ and a sheaf isomorphism $\theta:h_P\simeq F$. Because $P$ is itself an object of $T_{\mathrm{et}}$, set $\lambda_P=\theta_P(\mathrm{id}_P)$. Naturality gives $\theta_V(a)=a^{-1}\lambda_P$ for every etale $V\to T$ and $a:V\to P$ over $T$, using the inverse-image comparisons of Step 1.

source.place: Tag 03RV, lemma-characterize-finite-locally-constant; universal element evaluated at P

proof.text: For a trivializing chart $T_i$, the fibre-product property identifies $h_{P\times_TT_i}$ on $(T_i)_{\mathrm{et}}$ with $h_P|_{T_i}$. Under $\theta$ and $\tau_i$, this is $\underline G_{T_i}$. By [lem-galois-constant-sheaf-sets-representable], the latter is represented by $\coprod_{g\in G}T_i$. Both representing schemes are etale over $T_i$: for the first use [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change], and for the second apply [lem-sc-etale-coproduct-etale] to the finite family of identity maps (each identity is an open immersion, hence etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]). Yoneda [lem-galois-yoneda-fully-faithful] gives an isomorphism $P\times_TT_i\simeq\coprod_{g\in G}T_i$ under which the pulled-back universal frame on component $g$ is $\tau_i\circ g$. Indeed, its pullback along the component section is the image of that constant label under $\theta$. Since $1\in G$, this chart projection has a section. For every $t\in T$ choose a point of a covering chart over $t$ and then its point on the identity component; its image in $P$ lies over $t$. Thus $p$ is surjective.

Now let $v:U\to T$ be arbitrary, and put $P_U=P\times_TU$, $q:P_U\to U$. Pull $\lambda_P$ back to $P_U$ and use the constant-module comparison [lem-sfb-geometric-inverse-image-constant-module] and the composite inverse-image comparison [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image] to obtain $\lambda_{P_U}:\underline M_{P_U}\simeq q^{-1}v^{-1}H$. Pullback of this frame defines a morphism of sheaves on $U_{\mathrm{et}}$ from $h_{P_U}$ to the local isomorphism sheaf $F_{v^{-1}H}$: the source is a sheaf by [lem-weil-pbc-small-etale-representable-presheaf-sheaf], the target by [lem-sf-local-module-isom-sheaf]. Pull back the cover $\{T_i\to T\}$ to $U$: by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-base-change] the projections $U\times_TT_i\to U$ are etale and jointly surjective, hence a covering family of $U_{\mathrm{et}}$ as defined in [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. On $U_i=U\times_TT_i$, Step 4 base changes to $P_U\times_UU_i=\coprod_{g\in G}U_i$. This equality follows directly from the fibre-product universal property: by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], the inverse images of the disjoint open components partition the pullback and each is $U_i$. The frame on component $g$ is the pulled-back $\tau_i$ followed by the SAME constant $g$, by naturality in linear maps of the constant-module comparison. Thus the sheaf morphism is, on $U_i$, precisely the constant-$G$ isomorphism of Step 2 and [lem-galois-constant-sheaf-sets-representable]. It is locally injective and locally surjective, hence an isomorphism by [lem-galois-set-sheaf-local-bijection-isomorphism]. Evaluating at the final object $U$ gives $\operatorname{Mor}_T(U,P)=\operatorname{Mor}_U(U,P_U)\cong\operatorname{Fr}_H(U)$.

source.place: Tag 03Q1, lemma-stalk-pullback (4); Tag 03P5, remark-constant-locally-constant-maps; arbitrary-test-scheme extension by etale-local evaluation

proof.text: For $w:U'\to U$, the frame assigned to $a\circ w:U'\to P$ is the inverse image under $w$ of the frame assigned to $a:U\to P$, followed by the specified comparisons. This is the composition law of [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units], lifted to constant module sheaves by [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image]; constants carry the same linear maps by [lem-sfb-geometric-inverse-image-constant-module]. Hence Step 5's bijections are natural on all $T$-schemes. More generally, a map $W\to P_U$ over $U$ is exactly a map $W\to P$ over $T$ with its prescribed map $W\to U$. Step 5 identifies these with frames of $(W\to T)^{-1}H$, equivalently frames of $(W\to U)^{-1}v^{-1}H$. It sends the identity of $P_U$ to $\lambda_{P_U}$, proving the base-change representability assertion with its specified universal frame. For $U'\to U\to T$, both iterated base changes send a map from any $W$ to the inverse image of the SAME $\lambda_P$; the associativity equation in the cited composition lemma equates the two sheaf comparisons. The fibre-product associator equates the two maps of schemes. This proves compatibility with composition, rather than merely existence of an unspecified isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 03CB, sites-lemma-composition-morphisms-sites; Tag 03Q1, lemma-stalk-pullback (4); units and associativity

proof.text: For a geometric point $\bar t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$, Step 5 identifies the geometric fibre's set of points $\operatorname{Mor}_T(\operatorname{Spec}\Omega,P)$ with frames of $\bar t^{-1}H$. By [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-point-pullback-stalk], module sheaves on $(\operatorname{Spec}\Omega)_{\mathrm{et}}$ are equivalent, via global sections, to modules, and global sections of the pulled-back underlying abelian sheaf are $H_{\bar t}$. This identification is $A$-linear: naturality in the scalar endomorphisms and the constant-scalar comparison of [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image] identify each multiplication by $a\in A$. The constant source has global sections $A^n$, since the constant-module comparison is the equivalence's constant object. Thus these are exactly $\operatorname{Isom}_A(A^n,H_{\bar t})$, as claimed.

If $T$ is empty, any $T$-scheme is empty, any module sheaf on its small etale site is the unique zero sheaf (apply its sheaf condition to the empty covering), and all frame sets are singleton sets. The representing scheme $P$ is empty because it maps to $T$; surjectivity is vacuous. If $n=0$, then $G=\{1\}$ and all the preceding steps still apply. There is exactly one frame locally, and the sheaf condition makes $F$ terminal; the two representing etale objects $P$ and $T$ are isomorphic by Yoneda [lem-galois-yoneda-fully-faithful]. In particular no step used $n>0$, a nonempty or connected base, a characteristic restriction on $T$, or a Noetherian hypothesis.
